name: SomniGroup International Inc.
moat_justification: Leading premium brands (Tempur-Pedic, Sealy, Stearns & Foster) with proven pricing power — North America adjusted gross margin 61.8% in Q2 2026, consolidated gross margin held 40.3-44.6% over five years — plus vertical integration through Mattress Firm (Tempur Sealy brands >50% of its sales, 2,852 stores) and demonstrated share gains in a down industry. Against: ROIC proxy fell every year from 29.9% (2021) to 7.9% (2025, acquisition-inflated capital base; goodwill 39.6% of assets), mattresses have near-zero switching costs and are housing-linked discretionary, DTC/private-label rivals cap pricing, and the low-margin retail segment (~33% gross margin) dilutes the manufacturing franchise. Moderate/narrow moat.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 5.1%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 6.4x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (7.3%) vs bull-case tier C (11.0%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Good brands, moderate moat 5/10, now a levered retailer-manufacturer — at $63.58 it prices in the synergy/recovery story and returns only 8.8% weighted (IV@15% $31.29); clears 15% only at ~$31.
moat_for: #1 US bedding brands (Tempur-Pedic, Sealy, Stearns & Foster) with demonstrated premium pricing power
Vertical integration: Mattress Firm's 2,174 stores with Tempur Sealy brands >50% of sales — shelf control no rival has
Scale in manufacturing, logistics and ~$690M advertising across 2,852 stores in 100+ countries
Share gains in a declining industry (Mattress Firm same-store flat in Q1 2026 vs industry down mid-single digits)
moat_against: ROIC proxy down five straight years: 29.9% (2021) to 7.9% (2025); goodwill now 39.6% of assets
Deferrable, housing-linked discretionary product with near-zero switching costs
DTC and private-label competition caps pricing; other retailers remain multi-brand
Low-margin retail segment dilutes the manufacturing franchise; second integration (Leggett & Platt) stacked on the first
